subject: Variant sanity review and temporary version-lock request — NebulaApps trial
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria@nebulaapps.com>
Cc: Joe Park <joe@modelhub.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Variant sanity review and temporary version-lock request — NebulaApps trial

Hi team,

NebulaApps (Maria copied) is gearing up for a 6-week pilot starting May 3 and asked for a stable, pinned model endpoint for the duration of the pilot. The model in question is "lyra-70b-lite" (vendor: ModelHub) with two serving variants we currently have in catalog: lyra-70b-lite.fp16 and lyra-70b-lite.quant4. They want predictable latency and identical outputs across the pilot so they can integrate and run acceptance tests.

Asking for two things:
- An internal compat + safety sanity check for both variants (does quant4 produce acceptable diffs vs fp16 across our eval suite?). See attached intake + initial compat snapshot.
- A temporary version-lock (4–6 weeks) exception on the hosted route for NebulaApps while they run the pilot, with an automatic rollback/fallback plan if we detect regressions.

Constraints/notes:
- Customer is on a trial commit tied to DEAL-4387.
- We should avoid a permanent bypass of our compatibility gate — this would be an exception.
- Maria: please confirm whether NebulaApps needs data residency (they indicated US-only).

Dev/Rishi: can you confirm whether quant4 is safe to serve for production traffic and whether it requires runtime changes (KV cache tweaks, kernel selection)?
Laura: any compliance flags for a short-term version-lock on hosted endpoints?
Hannah: can you coordinate the rollout plan and monitoring dashboard?

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria@nebulaapps.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Variant sanity review and temporary version-lock request — NebulaApps trial

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> NebulaApps (Maria copied) is gearing up for a 6-week pilot starting May 3 and asked for a stable, pinned model endpoint for the duration of the pilot.

Quick technical readout from infra/serving side:
- We ran the vendor-supplied lyra-70b-lite.fp16 and lyra-70b-lite.quant4 across a small subset of our eval prompts (attached bench csv + compat report). Observations: quant4 yields ~2.8x memory savings and ~1.6x throughput vs fp16 on A100s, but output deltas are non-trivial on a minority (~6%) of prompts (long-form completion + codegen cases).
- The quant4 runtime path currently uses a different kernel fallback for rotary embeddings — that surfaced mismatch in top-k tokens on a few samples. Not a universal safety regression, but it could break acceptance tests that assert exact strings.
- KV-cache semantics are identical at RPC level, but we saw slight diff in prompt-prefix caching behavior that may affect cached response determinism for long chat histories.

Ask: if the customer requires byte-for-byte identical outputs to fp16, we should not recommend quant4 as the pinned variant. If they accept functional equivalence (small diffs tolerated), quant4 is a reasonable cost-saving option with a canary plan.

Operational proposal:
1) Temporarily allow a version-lock for the requested hosted route for NebulaApps for 4 weeks (not 6) with the following guardrails:
   - Canary at 5% traffic for first 48 hours comparing outputs with canonical fp16 variant.
   - Continuous drift monitor using our eval harness (alerts if top-3 token divergence > threshold on sample set).
   - Auto-fallback policy to lyra-70b-lite.fp16 if divergence triggers.
2) If customer insists on quant4 but also requires exact-matching, we should require them to run the acceptance suite in their environment and acknowledge residual risk.

Attachments: compat_report_20270422.pdf, benchmarks_lyra_variants_20270422.csv

I can own the canary config + drift monitor if we have sign-off.

— Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria@nebulaapps.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Variant sanity review and temporary version-lock request — NebulaApps trial

Vivek / team,

Thanks for the context. A few compliance / contractual notes for a hosted, time-limited version-lock:
- Timebox the exception explicitly in writing (e.g., 4 weeks) and include automatic expiry unless contract amendment is signed.
- Ensure audit logging at token/request level is retained for the pilot window (we should capture model version id, request id, timestamp).
- For US-only residency: confirm that logs and any persisted artifacts stay in US regions — Ops needs that parameter for s3/tooling.
- If NebulaApps wants us to maintain exact output parity (to the byte), require a signed acceptance of residual risk and removal of liability for subtle model mismatches.

I'll draft a short exception addendum language if we agree on guardrails. Also flagging that any pinned external-vendor model must have a signed EULA from ModelHub covering support and rollback SLAs.

Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria@nebulaapps.com>, procurement@nebulaapps.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Variant sanity review and temporary version-lock request — NebulaApps trial

Thanks all — agreed approach. Confirming internal approval for a temporary version-lock for NebulaApps with the following conditions (we'll capture in an exception ticket):
- Duration: 4 weeks from pilot start (May 3–May 31).
- Variant allowed: lyra-70b-lite.fp16 by default; lyra-70b-lite.quant4 allowed only if NebulaApps signs the residual-risk acknowledgement and accepts up to ~6% observed divergence on edge cases.
- Canary: 5% split to compare quant4 vs fp16 for first 48 hours when quant4 is enabled.
- Monitoring: Dev to enable drift monitor and automated rollback to fp16 if top-3 divergence threshold exceeded.
- Compliance: Laura will provide the addendum language; logs retained in US for the window.
- Rollout owner: Hannah, please schedule the canary launch and set dashboards; Vivek will coordinate customer comms.

Hannah — can you open the exception ticket (RED-1298) and book the rollout for first week of May? Maria/procurement — we'll circulate the addendum for signature today, and Rishi will confirm once the canary config is live.

— Rishi
Applied ML / Serving
Redwood Inference
